newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ parties hold post-election talks.
newsitem.headline: NZ parties hold post-election talks.

text.p: Negotiators for economic Nationalist New Zealand First and the main opposition Labour held talks on Tuesday in the wake of the inconclusive October 12 election and reported substantial progress.
But they were tight-lipped about which policy areas were discussed.
New Zealand First holds the balance of power after the election and is talking to both the ruling caretaker National Party and Labour over the shape of the new government.
All three parties have declined to put a deadline on the talks which are expected to last for several more weeks.
After Tuesday's meeting New Zealand First leader Winston Peters said: "We made substantial progress".
"We are going as hard and as fast as we we can," Peters told journalists, adding more talks with both Labour and National were set down for Wednesday and Thursday.
"We are trying to be fair and equal and non-prejudicial to both parties," he said.

Labour leader Helen Clark, who would be New Zealand's first woman prime minister if her party can strike a deal with Peters, said the parties had moved on to policy discussions after last week establishing protocols for the talks.
"We are just working our way through policy," she said.
Asked whether education and the economy were on the agenda as some media reports suggested Clark said: "We will keep that to ourselves."
Peters denied his party was the one which asked for the venue for the negotiating talks to be swept for bugs by the government's security service.
"We did not authorise, nor do we have the power to authorise such an investigation," Peters said.
Labour also denied it had asked for the sweep but traces of security seals were clearly evident on the doors as the negotiators arrived.
